faqs.q: Should I sign with a restoration company first?
faqs.a: Not before you know what the house is worth as-is. Assignment-of-benefits agreements can hand your claim to a contractor and limit your options. Get a cash offer first, then decide.

title: How Fast Can You Actually Sell a House? Every Option, Timed
desc: Seven days to seven months, depending on how you sell. Here's what actually sets the floor on each option, and what you can and can't compress.
answer: The fastest realistic sale is 7 days, to a cash buyer, when title is clear and the closing professional has availability. A cash sale with any title work typically runs 7–28 days. An iBuyer takes a few weeks. A listed, financed sale runs 30–60 days after you get an accepted offer, plus however long the house sits on market first. A short sale needs lender approval and typically runs 45–90 days. Probate adds months before anything can close at all.

p: Not the buyer's willingness. Three things: the title search, the closing professional's calendar, and any payoff or approval a third party controls.

A clean title on a house with one mortgage can be searched and cleared in days. A house with a judgment lien, an unreleased mortgage from a defunct lender, or a deceased co-owner on the deed cannot, no matter how motivated everyone is.

list: Cash buyer, clear title: 7–14 days
Cash buyer, ordinary title work: 14–28 days
iBuyer: a few weeks, if the property qualifies
Listed, financed buyer: 30–60 days after accepted offer, plus days on market
Short sale: 45–90 days, driven by the servicer
Probate sale: months before a personal representative is appointed, then a normal closing timeline

p: Have the payoff statements ordered early. Know your lender, your account number, and whether there are second liens. Locate the deed. If there's an HOA, request the estoppel letter as soon as you're under contract — associations are frequently the slowest party in a closing.
In attorney states (Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina), call the closing attorney the same day you accept an offer. Their calendar is often the binding constraint.
Probate appointment. Short sale approval. A quiet title action. A municipal lien search in a county that takes three weeks to produce one.
When you're racing a foreclosure sale date, these are what matter. Find out early which of them applies to you, because the answer determines whether a 7-day close is realistic or fantasy.
sections.callout: If you're up against a foreclosure sale date, the single most useful thing you can do today is order a title search and a payoff statement. Everything else in the timeline flexes. Those two don't.

p: A buyer promising to close in 48 hours is either not doing a title search or not telling you something. Both should worry you.
Seven days is fast and it's achievable. Faster than that generally means a step is being skipped, and the step being skipped is usually the one that protects you.

faqs.q: What's the fastest way to sell a house?
faqs.a: A cash buyer with clear title, typically 7 to 14 days. The floor is set by the title search and the closing attorney or title company's availability, not by the buyer's willingness.

faqs.q: How long does a normal listed sale take?
faqs.a: Commonly 30 to 60 days from accepted offer to closing on a financed deal, plus however long the house sits on the market before that offer arrives.

faqs.q: Why does title work take so long?
faqs.a: The search has to identify every recorded encumbrance and confirm the chain of ownership. Judgment liens, unreleased mortgages, and deceased co-owners still on the deed all take time to resolve, and none can be skipped.

faqs.q: Can I close in less than a week?
faqs.a: Occasionally, on a property with clear title and an available closing professional. Be skeptical of anyone promising it routinely — the step being skipped to get there is usually the one that protects you.

faqs.q: How much does probate delay a sale?
faqs.a: Months, typically, before the court appoints a personal representative with authority to sign the deed. You can sign a contract during that period and close once the appointment issues.
